entryDestinations.$comment: Semantic destinations of GET /api/v1/me/entry (SF-45, simplefit-api ADR 0017) -> canonical route per platform. Mobile has no sponsor surface: sponsor_application opens O05, whose approved Sponsor / Brand choice continues to the web partner application (SPX2); never the workspace chooser (A04), and no Sponsor capability or workspace is implied. coach_home (SF-51, SF-52, SF-53) opens the Coach home of each platform, today its canonical placeholder. context_selection opens the context chooser of each platform: WCX1 on the web (web.app.context, SF-54) and A04 on mobile (mobile.workspaces, SF-55); never role selection (WA6 / O05) or a home (D-ENTRY-CONTEXT-SELECTION). gym_home (SF-84) opens the GYM_WORKSPACE home of each platform: on the web the id-based gym console of the entry answer's gym_id (web.app.gyms._gym-id, SF-88, ADR 0026 D-G23), on mobile the id-based Gym pulse of the entry answer's gym_id (mobile.gyms._gym-id.pulse, SF-89). gym_selection (SF-84) opens the gym chooser of each platform: web.app.gyms on the web (SF-88) and mobile.gyms on mobile (SF-89), listing the entry answer's gym_workspaces; never a gym home or A04. gym_onboarding starts Gym setup, or resumes the owned draft named by gym_id.

discrepancies.sourceA: GymTabs (classes, members), CoachWebNav (fighters, programs, services), GymWebNav (challenges, sparring), AdminNav (support)
discrepancies.sourceB: Route Gallery: the targets need a parameter or open a creator; no list route exists
discrepancies.mismatch: Tabs/sidebar items point at /gym/classes/:classId/roster, /gym/members/:memberId, /app/coach/fighters/:fighterId, /app/coach/sessions/new, /app/coach/services/new, /app/gym/challenges/new, /app/gym/open-sparring/:openSparringId, /admin/support/:sessionId.
discrepancies.impact: A tab or sidebar item cannot open a route that needs an id it does not have.
discrepancies.resolution: Nav items for classes, members, coach fighters, open sparring and admin support point at design gaps; their detail routes are no longer NAV_ITEM.
discrepancies.decision: Creator routes stay valid nav targets. No default-resource navigation for routes that need an id. Missing list roots are design gaps.

discrepancies.title: Workspace routes carry no workspace identifier
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery: /app/gym/*, /app/coach/*, /sponsor/*, mobile /gym/*, /coach/*
discrepancies.sourceB: Identity model (User → WorkspaceMembership → Gym | Sponsor; a user may hold several)
discrepancies.mismatch: Paths do not say which gym or sponsor workspace they belong to (the gym console shows 'OWNER · 3 LOCATIONS').
discrepancies.impact: Links are only meaningful inside the active workspace; a user with two gym memberships cannot deep-link into a specific one.
discrepancies.resolution: No path change for the Sponsor workspace. The gym consoles are id-based (ADR 0026 D-G23): the web /app/gyms/:gymId/** since SF-88 and the mobile gym tabs /gyms/:gymId/** since SF-89, the id a lookup key that the backend authorizes on every request.
discrepancies.decision: The active workspace is session context. Workspace ids are not added to URLs globally; cross-workspace deep links may be added later when email/push features need them.

discrepancies.title: Fighter web routes have no role prefix
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 2/3: fighter web at /app/home, /app/board, …; coach at /app/coach/*, gym at /app/gym/*
discrepancies.sourceB: Identity model: no exclusive role
discrepancies.mismatch: /app and /app/home look role-neutral but are fighter screens.
discrepancies.impact: Coach-only or gym-only users must not land on fighter screens.
discrepancies.resolution: /app is an ENTRY route that redirects to the active workspace home (/app/home, /app/coach, /app/gym); /app/home requires FIGHTER. No path changes.

discrepancies.title: Account-level routes drawn on a persona page
discrepancies.sourceA: Design pages: Fighter Mobile §8 settings & account lifecycle, notifications, messages, search; Coach Mobile pricing, trials, billing; Desktop/Web 'Fighter settings', billing, checkout, payments, marketplace
discrepancies.sourceB: Identity model: settings, billing and messages belong to the User, not a role
discrepancies.mismatch: The page a screen sits on suggests a role that the route does not need (Messages is also the Coach 'Inbox' tab).
discrepancies.impact: Gating them by role would lock other roles out of their own account.
discrepancies.resolution: Classified SHARED: session AUTHENTICATED, no capability (mobile.shared / web.app.active shells). /settings/coach stays COACH. Backend authorization still decides per resource.

discrepancies.title: Trial and in-app pricing audience
discrepancies.sourceA: Coach Mobile §21–22 (/pricing?role=coach, /trial?state=…)
discrepancies.sourceB: Fighter Pro (/pro) and gym plan comparison (/pricing/compare?device=mobile on Gym Mobile)
discrepancies.mismatch: Trials are drawn for coaches only while pricing is shown to coaches and gyms.
discrepancies.impact: Unclear whether /trial is coach-only.
discrepancies.resolution: No change.

discrepancies.title: Lightweight account at checkout
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3 · QA1 Lightweight account · /checkout?account=quick
discrepancies.sourceB: Registry: /checkout is AUTHENTICATED
discrepancies.mismatch: QA1 implies checkout can start without a full account.
discrepancies.impact: Determines whether /checkout is reachable by guests.
discrepancies.resolution: mobile.checkout session PUBLIC; QA1 has condition NO_SESSION instead of ?account=quick.
discrepancies.decision: /checkout is publicly reachable. Without a session it renders the designed quick-account state (QA1). A normal SimpleFit identity and session must exist before any authenticated payment operation. No anonymous purchase model, no quick-account route.

discrepancies.title: Where the session starts during sign-up
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3 · O02 /signup → O03 /signup/verify → O04 /signup/consent → O05 /onboarding/role; web O02w /signup → WA3 /signup/account → WA4 /signup/verify; WA2 /login?step=workspace
discrepancies.sourceB: Guard model (GUEST_ONLY vs AUTHENTICATED)
discrepancies.mismatch: The design does not say at which step the user becomes authenticated; the workspace step of /login happens after authentication.
discrepancies.impact: Determines which sign-up steps redirect a signed-in user.
discrepancies.resolution: Access unchanged: sign-up and verify are GUEST_ONLY; consent and role are AUTHENTICATED/ONBOARDING.
discrepancies.decision: For email authentication the session begins after successful email verification. Consent and role onboarding run on an authenticated, onboarding-incomplete account. Social providers with provider-verified identities may transition differently; SF-22/SF-23 own those flows.

discrepancies.title: Admin access is outside the identity model
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 3/3 · AD0 Admin sign-in /admin/login (security key), AD0b Access scope /admin/access (support L2), AD9 two-person enforcement
discrepancies.sourceB: Canonical identity model: User → Identities, FighterProfile, CoachProfile, WorkspaceMembership (Gym, Sponsor)
discrepancies.mismatch: Admin staff, their sign-in and access scopes are not part of the identity tree.
discrepancies.impact: The ADMIN capability has no defined source.
discrepancies.resolution: capabilities.ADMIN.grantedBy updated. /admin/login stays GUEST_ONLY: it is an authentication entry surface. Authenticated admin entry, capability check, step-up and re-entry semantics are owned by the authentication/security implementation; no access class is added for them.
discrepancies.decision: Admin uses the same global User. Internal staff access is a backend-granted capability; no separate admin User model. Hardware-key/WebAuthn step-up and scoped admin sessions belong to later admin/auth implementation.

discrepancies.title: Sponsor-only and admin users on mobile
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery: sponsor portal and admin are web-only (WEB · PARTNERS, WEB · ADMIN)
discrepancies.sourceB: A04 Workspace switcher /workspaces shows '4 roles' on mobile
discrepancies.mismatch: No mobile destination for a user whose only workspace is a sponsor.
discrepancies.impact: The default-destination resolver has no mobile target.
discrepancies.resolution: capabilities.SPONSOR_WORKSPACE.mobile and ADMIN.mobile notes; guards.defaultDestinationFallback.mobile = mobile.workspaces.
discrepancies.decision: Sponsor workspaces may appear in mobile /workspaces with a 'continue on the web' action. No mobile Sponsor or Admin product surfaces.

discrepancies.title: Account lifecycle screens exist only on mobile
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3 · ST11–ST15 (/settings/delete/confirm, /account/pending-deletion, /account/suspended, /account/appeal)
discrepancies.sourceB: Route Gallery 2/3 · WS2 /app/settings/data?modal=delete (web)
discrepancies.mismatch: The web has no suspended, pending-deletion or appeal route.
discrepancies.impact: Web behaviour for restricted accounts is undefined.
discrepancies.resolution: Resolved by design version 1791276973-ad1d: WS3 /account/pending-deletion, WS4 /account/suspended and WS5 /account/appeal (WEB · ACCOUNT, shell web.account). The redirects that send restricted accounts there belong to the authentication/account lifecycle tickets.
discrepancies.decision: Web account-state and recovery surfaces must eventually be designed. Until the Route Gallery contains them, no web routes are invented; restricted-account behaviour is owned by auth/session handling.

discrepancies.title: Existing production routes differ from the design
discrepancies.sourceA: simplefit-platform: /[locale]/app (foundation page), [...rest] + not-found, /[locale]/dev/design-system
discrepancies.sourceB: simplefit-mobile: / (foundation home), (app)/app, +not-found, /dev/design-system
discrepancies.mismatch: Mobile / exists but is not yet LD1; web /app is a page while the design uses it as the entry that redirects (LD3); mobile /app is not in the gallery; /dev/design-system is developer-only on both platforms.
discrepancies.impact: IMPLEMENTED means the route resolves in production, not that its screen matches the artboard.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as IMPLEMENTED with a production note. Mobile /app is replaced when SF-33 builds the role groups; /dev/design-system is classified INTERNAL. Screens are implemented by their feature tickets. SF-43 replaced the web / foundation landing with L1 (LandHome).

discrepancies.title: Mobile /gym and /coach mix two audiences
discrepancies.sourceA: Fighter-facing: /gym/:gymId/community, /gym/:gymId/classes/:classId/book, /gym/:gymId/memberships(/:membershipId), /gym/:gymId/store, /coach/:coachId/services/:serviceId
discrepancies.sourceB: Workspace screens: /gym/pulse, /gym/check-in, /gym/classes/:classId/roster, /gym/members/:memberId, /gym/staff/on-shift, /coach/today, /coach/fighters, …
discrepancies.mismatch: One URL prefix serves fighters (public resources) and the gym/coach workspace.
discrepancies.impact: A layout guard on the /gym or /coach folder would lock fighters out.
discrepancies.resolution: Paths kept as designed. Expo Router matches static segments before dynamic ones and ids are opaque, so there is no runtime collision. Guards are attached per route through route groups, never by URL prefix (§12).

discrepancies.title: Rows that reuse another screen's artboard
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3: 'Coach · Account' /onboarding/coach?step=account → SignUp.dc.html; 'Fighter · Boxing profile' step=profile → OnbFExperience.dc.html (also OF2 Experience); OF1 'Account' → OnbFProfile.dc.html; Friends / Friend Requests → Feed.dc.html
discrepancies.sourceB: The artboards' own titles
discrepancies.mismatch: The screen name and the artboard it opens disagree.
discrepancies.impact: A visual ticket may build the wrong screen for a wizard step.
discrepancies.resolution: Two alias rows moved to excludedRows; x-mobile-friends / x-mobile-friend-requests renamed S04 / S05. OF1 'Account' (OnbFProfile.dc.html, 'Your fighter profile') was not a mismatch.
discrepancies.decision: Mobile wizards use the coded keys (fighter OF2 = ?step=experience); the duplicate ?step=profile alias is dropped. Web keeps its own presentation keys. Coach 'account' is not a role onboarding step: global account creation happens first. The Friends screens are S04/S05. Backend onboarding step ids are a separate API contract.

discrepancies.title: Program builder appears under two paths
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3 · CRW2 Product tour · /app/coach/programs/new?tour=2 (FirstRunWebCTour.dc.html)
discrepancies.sourceB: Route Gallery 2/3 · WC3 Shared Session Creator · /app/coach/sessions/new?assign=shared (WebProgramBuilder.dc.html); CoachWebNav 'Programs & sessions' → WebProgramBuilder
discrepancies.mismatch: /app/coach/programs/new exists only as a first-run tour state.
discrepancies.impact: Possibly one builder with two paths.
discrepancies.resolution: Route web.app.coach.programs.new removed; CRW2 moved to web.app.coach.sessions.new.
discrepancies.decision: /app/coach/sessions/new is canonical; the first-run tour is ?tour=2 on it. /app/coach/programs/new is dropped. Frontend route names need not mirror backend resource names.

discrepancies.title: Find sparring is marked future
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3 · 9.17 S22 Find sparring (future) · /sparring/find, state 'future'
discrepancies.sourceB: Implementation status model
discrepancies.mismatch: The design approves the route but labels it future scope.
discrepancies.impact: A placeholder would expose an unplanned feature.
discrepancies.resolution: Kept in the registry as DEFERRED (not removed, not a placeholder).

discrepancies.title: Backend API surface is proposed, not the contract
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 3/3 · 'Backend · API surface (proposed)': 31 rows, 32 endpoints
discrepancies.sourceB: simplefit-api/openapi/simplefit.api.json (GET /api/health) and router.ex (/api/openapi, /api/docs)
discrepancies.mismatch: None of the 32 proposed endpoints exists. Some forms need review against ADR 0003 (GET /api/v1/board?mode=:mode with a query in the route, custom-method suffixes rounds:batch and members:import, the .pdf extension on invoices).
discrepancies.impact: Treating the design list as the API contract would add speculative endpoints.
discrepancies.resolution: All 32 are DEFERRED inventory. Each is added to OpenAPI only by the feature ticket that needs it; OpenAPI stays canonical. SF-31 changes nothing in simplefit-api.

discrepancies.title: Email previews and share images
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 3/3 · E01–E16 /api/v1/emails/E0x/preview?locale=en; 'Share card images' /og/:type/:id.png
discrepancies.sourceB: docs/design-handoff.md §6: email production owner not decided; router: no /og scope
discrepancies.mismatch: Server-rendered outputs with paths but no owner; /og is outside /api.
discrepancies.impact: Not UI routes for either client.
discrepancies.resolution: Registered under 'outputs' as DEFERRED. The ticket that implements email or share images decides owner and path.

discrepancies.title: Route Gallery lives on a reference-only page
discrepancies.sourceA: docs/design-handoff.md §1/§6 and docs/design-source.json: pitch-business is 'reference only; never implemented'
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-31: the Route Gallery (pitch-business) is the IA source
discrepancies.mismatch: The handoff contract excluded the page that now defines routes.
discrepancies.impact: Future readers could ignore the Route Gallery.
discrepancies.resolution: The handoff contract now names the three Route Gallery artboards as the IA source for routes. They are never implemented visually; the rest of the page stays reference only.

discrepancies.title: Web 404 is tagged as site only
discrepancies.sourceA: Route Gallery 1/3 · 35.6 ER2 '404 · catch-all' tagged WEB · SITE
discrepancies.sourceB: The same row's path: /* → 404 (site · app · sponsor · admin)
discrepancies.mismatch: Tag and path disagree on scope.
discrepancies.impact: None for routing.
discrepancies.resolution: One web catch-all (web.not-found) for every area; an area may render the not-found state inside its own shell.

discrepancies.title: Canvas changed since the SF-16 audit
discrepancies.sourceA: docs/design-source.json audit: version 1791206633-31de, 456 artboards
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-31 reads: 1791271288-f2e9 (462 artboards), then 1791276973-ad1d (473 artboards)
discrepancies.mismatch: Six artboards were added after SF-16, and eleven more in the route-gap design pass (1791276973-ad1d, 11 new Route Gallery rows).
discrepancies.impact: None for SF-31: every product-page artboard is referenced by the Route Gallery except Flow, Route and sheet boards.
discrepancies.resolution: The registry records the version it was reconciled against (source.version). The SF-16 audit block in design-source.json is not rewritten.

discrepancies.title: Coach web 'Invite fighters' links a mobile invite screen
discrepancies.sourceA: WebCoachFighters.dc.html (WC7, /app/coach/fighters): action 'Invite fighters'
discrepancies.sourceB: Canvas target InviteCoach.dc.html: mobile INV1 'Invites · coach / gym / friend' at /invite/:code
discrepancies.mismatch: The web action targets a mobile artboard. It is not established that the Coach → Fighter invitation on web is the same flow as INV1, which a recipient uses to accept a coach, gym or friend invite.
discrepancies.impact: Building it from INV1 could merge two relationship directions (coach invites fighter vs fighter receives/uses a coach invite) into one route and screen.
discrepancies.resolution: Claude Design 1792151007-1d70 (SF-60) adds WFI1, the web page of the E08 link (/invite/coach#token=…): web.invite.coach, where the recipient reviews and accepts or declines over the SF-57 API. The coach's own invitation stays the in-page composer on WC7 (SF-58). INV1 is the mobile artboard and stays deferred (D-MOBILE-FIGHTER-COACH-INVITATIONS).

discrepancies.title: Web Fighter onboarding reduced to the backend-supported steps
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design 1791399145-48dd (Version 75): WF0 Profile basics → WF1 Boxing profile → WF6 Complete; WF2 Gym, WF3 Coach, WF4 Privacy, WF5 Notifications grouped as FUTURE — NOT IN CURRENT PRODUCTION FLOW
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-25 backend (ADR 0015): FighterProfile persists the WF0 and WF1 fields only; no Gym, Coach, privacy-settings or notification-preferences domain exists
discrepancies.mismatch: The earlier web flow had six steps; four of them have no owning backend domain, the WF0 fields (required for completion) had no web step, and the route required the FIGHTER capability that only a FighterProfile can grant.
discrepancies.impact: Building WF2-WF5 would fake persistence or cross-client resume; requiring FIGHTER before the route that creates the FighterProfile is circular.
discrepancies.resolution: Current screens WF0 (?step=basics), WF1 (?step=profile) and WF6 (?step=complete). WF2-WF5 stay registered as gallery rows with status DEFERRED. The route needs an authenticated session only (capability null, phase ONBOARDING); Fighter intent travels as the ephemeral ?intent=fighter parameter resolved by GET /api/v1/me/entry (D-ENTRY-RESOLUTION), never a user role. The step query is navigation only: resume and completion come from the backend profile state.
discrepancies.decision: Web Fighter onboarding follows the SF-25 backend scope; WF2-WF5 return with their owning domains.

discrepancies.title: Post-authentication entry is resolved by the backend
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design 1791448557-b0b9 (Version 78): WA5 Account basics & consent (/app/onboarding/account) and WA6 Choose where to start (/app/onboarding/role); RouteAuth, FlowAuthModel and FlowWebRoute: auth -> account basics if incomplete -> explicit intent if present -> otherwise role selection -> role journey; Google / Apple never imply Fighter
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-24 clients: resolveEntry(viewer, returnTo) = a valid returnTo, otherwise the neutral entry; GET /api/me carries only the viewer id
discrepancies.mismatch: The design routes every authenticated entry through account registration and role intent; the clients only knew returnTo and the app root, and web had no account-basics or role-selection route.
discrepancies.impact: Without one resolver, web and mobile would each re-derive registration and onboarding state, and generic provider sign-up would drift towards Fighter.
discrepancies.resolution: GET /api/v1/me/entry (simplefit-api ADR 0017) returns a semantic destination derived from persisted state; guards.entryDestinations maps it to one route per platform. Intent is the allow-listed, ephemeral guards.intentParam query parameter, never stored and never a capability. Mandatory destinations (account_registration, fighter_onboarding) win over a safe returnTo, which is kept as the continuation. Web adds WA5 and WA6; mobile maps to O04 and O05.
discrepancies.decision: One backend entry resolver for all providers and both platforms; intent is navigation only.

discrepancies.title: Onboarding entry routes required the capability they create
discrepancies.sourceA: Route registry: web.app.onboarding.coach (COACH), web.app.onboarding.gym (GYM_WORKSPACE), mobile.onboarding.fighter (FIGHTER), mobile.onboarding.coach (COACH), mobile.onboarding.gym (GYM_WORKSPACE)
discrepancies.sourceB: Capability model: FIGHTER is granted by a FighterProfile, COACH by a CoachProfile, GYM_WORKSPACE by a workspace membership; those are created by these very onboarding routes
discrepancies.mismatch: A user without the capability could never reach the route that grants it.
discrepancies.impact: Onboarding would be unreachable, or clients would have to fake the capability.
discrepancies.resolution: Onboarding entry routes need an authenticated session only (capability null, phase ONBOARDING), like web.app.onboarding.fighter (D-WEB-FIGHTER-ONBOARDING-FLOW). Post-onboarding application routes keep their capability. Intent is not authorization.
discrepancies.decision: Onboarding entry routes never require the capability they create.

discrepancies.title: WA3 shows consent checkboxes before authentication
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design WebRegAccount (WA3): 'I accept the Terms and Privacy Policy', 'I am 16 or older' and product news checkboxes on the pre-authentication create-account step
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-44 (simplefit-api ADR 0016) and Claude Design WA5: consents are recorded with their document version after authentication, through the account registration API
discrepancies.mismatch: Two consent surfaces; only the post-authentication one can be persisted.
discrepancies.impact: Persisting or trusting the WA3 checkboxes would create a second, unversioned consent record.
discrepancies.resolution: SF-36: WA3 keeps the artboard's three consent checkboxes and the full name in place, disabled and unchecked (the name field says it is added after verifying). Only the email address is submitted; nothing is collected, validated or stored before a User exists. WA5 (account_registration) owns full name, date of birth, Terms and Privacy acceptance and the optional product news.

discrepancies.title: Web Coach onboarding reduced to the backend-supported steps
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design 1791896379-65b7 (Version 87): WCR1 Coach profile (?step=profile) -> WCR2 Coaching type (?step=type) -> WCR7 Complete (?step=complete); WCR3 Credentials, WCR4 Business size, WCR5 Gym and WCR6 Plan marked FUTURE (verification, gym and billing domains)
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-50 backend (ADR 0020): CoachProfile persists display_name, brand_name, country_code, city, bio, languages, coaching_formats and competition_levels; completion needs display_name, country_code, city, at least one coaching format and the account registration. No verification, gym-membership or billing domain exists
discrepancies.mismatch: The earlier web flow had seven steps; four of them have no owning backend domain.
discrepancies.impact: Building WCR3-WCR6 would fake persistence, verification, gym relationships or billing.
discrepancies.resolution: Current screens WCR1, WCR2 and WCR7. WCR3-WCR6 stay registered as gallery rows with status DEFERRED. The route needs an authenticated session only (D-ONBOARDING-ENTRY-CAPABILITY); Coach intent travels as the ephemeral ?intent=coach parameter. The step query is navigation only: resume and completion come from GET /api/v1/me/coach-profile, and completion only from POST /api/v1/me/coach-profile/complete-onboarding. The coach name may be pre-filled with the account's full name only as an editable, unsaved suggestion for a new profile. WCR7 continues through an explicit Coach context choice (PUT /api/v1/me/entry/context) and the entry resolver (coach_home), never to an invented workspace.
discrepancies.decision: Web Coach onboarding follows the SF-50 backend scope; WCR3-WCR6 return with their owning domains.

discrepancies.title: Web Gym owner registration reduced to the backend-supported steps
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design 1792675284-1046 (GYM 5e): a 14-step setup (OG1 Gym name & type with a public handle, OG2 several locations, OG3 Branding with logo, cover, public URL and a verified badge, OG4 Gym size, OG5 Features, OG6 Plan and trial, OG6b Registration complete with an active trial, OG7-OG14 verification, memberships, payments, timetable, team, import, community and publishing)
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-83/SF-84/SF-85 backend (ADR 0026): createGym (name, gym_type, idempotent client_request_id), getGymSetup / updateGymSetup (name, gym_type, phone, website, tagline, accent_color; required expected_revision), setGymPrimaryLocation (one primary location; required expected_revision) and completeGymSetup (name, gym_type and a primary location; account registration). No handle, media, sizing, entitlement, billing, verification, staff invitation, member, timetable or publishing domain exists
discrepancies.mismatch: Three of the fourteen steps are backed (partly: no handle, single location, no media); eleven have no owning domain, and OG6b claimed a trial and a plan.
discrepancies.impact: Building OG4-OG14, the handle, extra locations or uploads would fake persistence, billing, verification or publication.
discrepancies.resolution: Approved SF-86 differences: a three-step progress (Gym name & type, Location, Branding) with OG4-OG14 shown as coming later, never links; no public handle or URL; one location; OG3 Logo and Cover shown as not available yet (no fake upload) and a real Skip; no verified, trial or plan copy; OG3's primary action 'Create gym' calls completeGymSetup; OG6b says 'Gym created' and continues with 'Go to gym' through an explicit Gym context choice (PUT /api/v1/me/entry/context with gym_id) and the entry resolver (gym_home). The step query is navigation only: the draft comes from GET /api/v1/me/gyms, resume and completion from the gym setup. The route needs an authenticated session only (D-ONBOARDING-ENTRY-CAPABILITY). Claude Design keeps the 14-step artboards and is reconciled separately.
discrepancies.decision: Web Gym owner registration follows the SF-83-SF-85 backend scope; OG4-OG14 return with their owning domains.

discrepancies.title: Mobile Gym owner registration built natively without mobile artboards
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design 1792675284-1046 (GYM 4): mobile owner onboarding is only OG0 'Gym owner · continue on web' (OnbGHandoff), a handoff with an emailed setup link and code; SF-82 (03-registration-workspace-lifecycle §4, 07-routing) planned owner creation on the web only
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-87 (approved 2026-10-27): native Gym owner registration on mobile on the same SF-83/SF-84/SF-85 contract as the web (SF-86); the API is client-agnostic (ADR 0026)
discrepancies.mismatch: No mobile OG1-OG3/OG6b artboards exist, and OG0 describes a handoff that SF-87 replaces; OG0's link and code would be a new sign-in credential (ADR 0012).
discrepancies.impact: Without a decision the mobile route would stay a placeholder or show a handoff the product no longer wants.
discrepancies.resolution: Approved SF-87 differences: OG1 -> OG2 -> OG3 -> OG6b built natively on the approved mobile onboarding frame (Claude Design COACH 3, 390 x 844: back button, 'Step n of 3', segmented progress, heading, scrolling body, pinned actions) with the web OG content and every SF-86 approved difference (three steps, OG4-OG14 never shown, no handle or public URL, one location, Logo and Cover not available yet, no verified, trial or plan copy, 'Create gym' and 'Skip for now' on OG3, OG6b 'Gym created' and 'Go to gym' through the SF-84 entry). Save & exit saves and returns through the entry, or to Settings when the draft is the only context. OG0 is superseded and stays a DEFERRED gallery row. The route needs an authenticated session only (D-ONBOARDING-ENTRY-CAPABILITY). Mobile OG artboards are added to Claude Design separately (the canvas is at its file limit).
discrepancies.decision: Owners can register a gym on mobile with the web's steps; Claude Design gains the mobile artboards later.

discrepancies.title: Mobile Coach onboarding reduced to the backend-supported steps
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design up to 1791965411-694c: OC1-OC11 (eleven steps) with years coaching, boxing background, formats mixed with competition levels and Strength & Conditioning, credentials, business size, gym, plan and trial, services, payouts, fighter invitations, coach data rules and a completion screen showing a trial, licence review, services, payouts and an invite link
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-50 backend (ADR 0020): CoachProfile persists display_name, brand_name, country_code, city, bio, languages, coaching_formats (personal_training, group_coaching, online_coaching, fight_camps) and competition_levels (amateur, professional); completion needs display_name, country_code, city, at least one coaching format and the account registration. No verification, gym, billing, services, payouts, invitation or privacy-sharing domain exists
discrepancies.mismatch: Two of the eleven mobile steps were partly backed; eight had no owning domain, and the completion screen showed records that do not exist.
discrepancies.impact: Building OC3-OC10 or the old OC11 would fake persistence, verification, billing, relationships or consent.
discrepancies.resolution: Claude Design 1791966129-8ecb (Version 89, SF-53) reconciles OC1 (coach name, brand, country, city, bio, coaching languages), OC2 (coaching formats; competition levels as a separate optional group) and OC11 (the saved profile only, and 'Coach tools are not available yet'); OC3-OC10 are FUTURE gallery rows with status DEFERRED and never part of the flow (a FUTURE ?step= resolves to the resume step). The route needs an authenticated session only (D-ONBOARDING-ENTRY-CAPABILITY); the Coach workspace (mobile.coach) renders only when the entry reports COACH. OC11 continues through the explicit Coach context choice and the entry (coach_home), never to an invented workspace.
discrepancies.decision: Mobile Coach onboarding follows the SF-50 backend scope, as the web (D-WEB-COACH-ONBOARDING-FLOW); OC3-OC10 return with their owning domains.

discrepancies.title: The context_selection entry destination has a chooser on each platform
discrepancies.sourceA: simplefit-api SF-51 (ADR 0017 amendment): GET /api/v1/me/entry may answer context_selection (both profiles in progress, or both completed without a last explicit choice); PUT /api/v1/me/entry/context records an explicit choice between completed contexts
discrepancies.sourceB: Claude Design 1791982482-71e3 (SF-54): WCX1 Choose where to continue (web) and the context switcher in the Fighter and Coach sidebars. Claude Design 1791994719-673f (SF-55): A04 reconciled as 'One account, every role' (switch, choose and setup modes; pending and failed states). WA6 (web.app.onboarding.role) and O05 (mobile.onboarding.role) start a journey by intent; they do not choose between completed contexts
discrepancies.mismatch: Before SF-55 the destination had a web route but no mobile route.
discrepancies.impact: Mapping it to WA6 / O05 would present journey selection as a context switcher; mapping it to a home would guess the user's context.
discrepancies.resolution: context_selection maps to web.app.context (WCX1) on the web and to mobile.workspaces (A04) on mobile. Completed contexts are opened by recording the SF-51 choice; unfinished journeys are continued with an explicit intent and never recorded. A user with both profiles opens either workspace directly: workspace gates check the capability, not the last chosen context. On mobile the same A04 chooser is a sheet from the Fighter and Coach home identity pills.
discrepancies.decision: The web chooser is WCX1 (SF-54); the mobile chooser is A04 (SF-55).

discrepancies.title: Mobile gym owner first run built on measured native targets from the four MVP tour steps
discrepancies.sourceA: Claude Design 112 (1793198527-a0fc): GR1 FirstRunGPulse (states not_started, in_progress, pending, failed, skip_confirm, completed, dismissed, loading, error, offline, session_expired, revoked; the five-item opening checklist; a fixed 390 × 1060 frame) and GR2 FirstRunGCheckinTip (four MVP steps, done, finishing, finish_failed and confirm, drawn at artboard coordinates; six FUTURE steps)
discrepancies.sourceB: SF-90 backend: GET /api/v1/gyms/{gym_id}/first-run (status unavailable, not_started, in_progress, completed or dismissed; checklist create_gym, add_class, invite_staff, invite_members, first_check_in with completed, available or coming_later), POST start, complete and dismiss with an empty body; owner only (manage_first_run), 403 for other staff, 404 for foreign or revoked gyms, 409 with the kept outcome
discrepancies.mismatch: The artboards place the rings and cards at fixed coordinates of one tall frame and include steps for domains that do not exist; production lays out from 375 to 430 pt, with dynamic type, and scrolls.
discrepancies.impact: Copying coordinates would point at the wrong place on every other phone, text size or scroll position; building the FUTURE steps would point at features that do not exist.
discrepancies.resolution: SF-92: GR1 and GR2 follow Claude Design 112 on the real Gym pulse (no own route). Every ring is the measured target in window coordinates, re-measured on step change, rotation, text size, page reflow and return to the foreground; content targets are scrolled into view first; a target that cannot be measured gets no ring or arrow and the card stays on screen. The coach mark uses the opposite theme's tokens as FR5. 'Your gym is ready' shows only when the API reports create_gym completed. The skip confirmation is a bottom sheet. Android Back goes one step back, asks before ending on step 1 and never records. A lost answer to Finish or End is reconciled by reading the state again. The completed and dismissed notices show only on the screen that kept the outcome; there is no tour replay. The FUTURE steps are not built.
discrepancies.decision: Build the approved four-step tour on measured native targets and the API's checklist only; FUTURE steps wait for their domains.
